gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Prusa rates the nozzles on its CORE One+ INDX tools (0.4 mm high-flow, surface-hardened nitrocarburized steel) as 'not designed for long-term printing with abrasive materials': each lasts about 10 kg of PETG-CF, 5 kg of PC-CF or 0.5 kg of Prusament Ultraglow before print quality is affected.
standout_why: I compared against both pages ChatGPT cited. goodprints3d.com (2026-05-14) says only that the P2S includes 'hardened-steel extrusion hardware' and has 'supported-filament boundaries', but never lists them. It gives no filament limits and no nozzle type for the Prusa CORE One. 3dprinterlab.net (2026-06-13) says Bambu doesn't recommend abrasive filament on the P1S's stock hardware, and that the A1 'does not solve ABS, ASA'. It never mentions the Prusa CORE One+ and gives no lifetime for a nozzle on carbon-filled filament. ChatGPT's own table ends with 'PA-CF … with appropriate printing equipment' and never says what that equipment is or which of its three cards has it. Neither cited page names a multi-material add-on for QIDI or Prusa, or what that add-on needs.
decides: This qualifies the pick rather than overturning it. Someone buying the Prusa CORE One+ to print carbon-filled parts should know that Prusa's own figure for its hardened INDX nozzle is about 5 kg of PC-CF. That makes the nozzle a part you replace, not a fixture. The QIDI Q2 ($449 on qidi3d.com, down from $649) costs the same as ChatGPT's $449 P2S card. QIDI lists a 370 °C nozzle and 65 °C active chamber heating, and the Q2 works with the QIDI Box ($228). That makes the Q2 the stronger fit at $449 for PA and CF parts. I couldn't open a Bambu page to confirm the P2S's own nozzle and AMS limits.
